title: Chess experts remember game positions better than scrambled ones
body: In experiments, strong chess players recall more of a briefly shown position than weaker players. Their advantage is greater for positions from games than for randomly placed pieces, where familiar relationships are less common.
takeaway: To remember a complex scene, learn the patterns that connect its parts.
visual: a chessboard with pieces placed in a recognisable midgame formation

title: An object's usual job can hide another use for it
body: In Karl Duncker's candle problem, a small box could be pinned to a wall as a shelf. Solvers had more difficulty seeing that use when the box was presented full of tacks rather than empty.
takeaway: If you are stuck, describe the object's shape or material before naming what it is usually for.
source: German and Defeyter, Psychonomic Bulletin & Review (2000)
visual: a small box used as a candle shelf on a plain wall
